title.zh: 镜端双极损失电势闭合

summary: Evaluate source-equivalent one-way ion/electron end-loss fluxes at a prescribed plug potential, or solve their charge-weighted flux balance independently on each flux surface with bounded bracket expansion and bisection.

identity.relation: Single-ion mirror end-loss fluxes and ambipolar plug potential relative to a reference surface
identity.direction: (reference/plug fields, psi, ion mass/charge, reference densities, ion/electron thermal energies, potentials, refill and solver controls) -> plug potential, one-way particle fluxes and current-balance diagnostics
identity.definition: For each species form a one-way half-space flux n*sqrt(T_parallel/(2*pi*m))*I(s,a)*refill, where s=(T_perpendicular/T_parallel)*(B_plug/B_reference-1) and a=q*(phi_plug-phi_reference)/T_parallel; I is the implemented piecewise mirror/electrostatic barrier pitch integral. Electrons use a fixed electron mass, charge -e and equal parallel/perpendicular thermal energies; ion charge state is q_i/e. In evaluate mode calculate fluxes at phi_plug_v without solving. In solve mode seek charge_state*ion_flux=electron_flux using a log-current ratio, an initial phi_reference +/- initial_bracket_thermal*(T_i_parallel/q_i+T_e/e) bracket, at most eight expansion rounds, then shared vectorized bisection up to max_iterations. Joint zero-density surfaces keep phi_reference_v.
identity.model: One magnetized positive ion species and an electron half-space mirror/electrostatic end-loss model, with caller-supplied reference populations and phenomenological loss-refill fractions; not a full collisional transport or self-consistent equilibrium model.
identity.geometry: Independent caller-defined flux surfaces with reference and plug magnetic magnitudes; scalar or array values share one NumPy broadcast shape.
identity.coordinates: psi identifies the caller's surfaces and is passed to optional density/temperature/potential profile callables. No psi monotonicity, spatial coordinate alignment or field-line geometry is checked.
identity.boundary: The reference potential phi_reference_v fixes the voltage origin; the unknown plug potential is solved relative to it. In solve mode both reference densities must be positive together or zero together per surface; joint vacuum retains phi_reference_v. In evaluate mode a prescribed phi_plug_v is required and current balance is not imposed.
assumptions: B_reference and B_plug are positive magnitudes in tesla; thermal-energy inputs in joules and charge in coulombs describe the same single-ion/electron system.

The reference profiles and mirror ratio represent compatible surfaces, and each species' one-way flux is adequately described by the implemented half-space barrier integral and chosen refill fraction.
The electron reference density defaults to (ion_charge_c/e)*ion_density_ref_m3 but may be supplied independently; evaluate mode accepts nonneutral and one-sided-vacuum states for diagnosis.

inputs.name: b_reference_t
inputs.shape: scalar or array; jointly broadcast with b_plug_t, psi and phi_reference_v
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive at every surface.

inputs.name: b_plug_t
inputs.shape: scalar or array; common broadcast shape
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive at every surface; the implementation does not require b_plug_t >= b_reference_t.

inputs.name: psi
inputs.shape: scalar or array; common broadcast shape
inputs.constraints: Finite; no monotonicity or normalization requirement is enforced.

inputs.name: ion_mass_kg
inputs.description: Mass of the positive ion species.

inputs.name: ion_charge_c
inputs.description: Positive ion charge; divided by elementary charge to form the charge-state multiplier.
inputs.constraints: Strictly positive; integer charge state is not enforced.

inputs.name: ion_density_ref_m3
inputs.description: Ion reference number density, optionally a callable of psi.
inputs.shape: scalar, array or callable output broadcastable to common shape
inputs.dtype: real array-like or Python callable returning real array-like
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative. In solve mode it must be positive exactly where electron reference density is positive.

inputs.name: ion_temperature_parallel_j
inputs.description: Ion parallel thermal-energy scale, optionally a callable of psi.
inputs.shape: scalar, array or callable output broadcastable to common shape
inputs.dtype: real array-like or Python callable returning real array-like

inputs.name: ion_temperature_perpendicular_j
inputs.description: Ion perpendicular thermal-energy scale, optionally a callable of psi.
inputs.shape: scalar, array or callable output broadcastable to common shape
inputs.dtype: real array-like or Python callable returning real array-like

inputs.name: electron_temperature_j
inputs.description: Electron thermal-energy scale used in both pitch directions, optionally a callable of psi.
inputs.shape: scalar, array or callable output broadcastable to common shape
inputs.dtype: real array-like or Python callable returning real array-like

inputs.name: phi_reference_v
inputs.description: Reference potential and returned potential on joint-vacuum surfaces in solve mode.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; common broadcast shape
inputs.constraints: Finite; the solve bracket is centered on this field.

inputs.name: electron_density_ref_m3
inputs.description: Optional electron reference density, or callable of psi.
inputs.shape: scalar, array or callable output broadcastable to common shape
inputs.dtype: real array-like or Python callable returning real array-like
inputs.constraints: If absent, charge_state times ion_density_ref_m3 is used; if supplied, finite and nonnegative. Solve mode requires paired positive or paired zero density on each surface.

inputs.name: ion_loss_refill
inputs.description: Multiplier of the modeled one-way ion loss flux.
inputs.constraints: In [0,1]; solve mode requires strictly positive value, while evaluate mode permits zero.

inputs.name: electron_loss_refill
inputs.description: Multiplier of the modeled one-way electron loss flux.

inputs.name: potential_tolerance_v
inputs.description: Maximum active change between consecutive bisection midpoints for convergence.
inputs.constraints: Strictly positive; used together with current_tolerance.

inputs.name: current_tolerance
inputs.description: Maximum absolute log-current ratio at the tested midpoint.
inputs.constraints: Strictly positive; a separate relative_current_residual is returned for diagnosis.

inputs.name: max_iterations
inputs.description: Maximum number of shared vectorized bisection updates.
inputs.dtype: Python or NumPy integer scalar, excluding bool
inputs.constraints: Integer >= 1; float values are not truncated.

inputs.name: initial_bracket_thermal
inputs.description: Initial bracket half-width in combined ion/electron thermal voltages.
inputs.constraints: Strictly positive; expansion is additionally bounded to eight rounds.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Choose plug-potential solve or prescribed-potential flux evaluation.

inputs.name: phi_plug_v
inputs.description: Prescribed plug potential for evaluate mode, optionally a callable of psi.
inputs.shape: scalar, array or callable output broadcastable to common shape
inputs.dtype: real array-like or Python callable returning real array-like
inputs.constraints: Required and finite in evaluate mode. Ignored in solve mode.

outputs.name: potential_v
outputs.description: Solved or prescribed plug potential; joint-vacuum surfaces retain phi_reference_v in solve mode.
outputs.constraints: Evaluate mode returns supplied phi_plug_v; solve mode returns only after all active surfaces meet the implemented stopping test.

outputs.name: ion_particle_flux_m2_s
outputs.description: Modeled one-way ion end-loss particle flux after ion_loss_refill.
outputs.constraints: Zero for zero ion density or zero ion_loss_refill; no post-computation finiteness check.

outputs.name: electron_particle_flux_m2_s
outputs.description: Modeled one-way electron end-loss particle flux after electron_loss_refill.
outputs.constraints: Zero for zero electron density; no post-computation finiteness check.

outputs.name: log_current_ratio
outputs.description: Log of charge-state-weighted ion flux minus log of electron flux, each floored at float64 tiny.
outputs.constraints: A floor-dependent numerical diagnostic when a flux vanishes; zero for joint vacuum.

outputs.name: relative_current_residual
outputs.description: Charge-state-weighted ion flux minus electron flux divided by their sum floored at float64 tiny.
outputs.constraints: Evaluate mode need not be balanced; joint vacuum gives zero. The solve stopping test uses log_current_ratio at the preceding midpoint, not this final residual.

outputs.name: iterations
outputs.description: Shared bisection update count, or zero in evaluate mode.
outputs.constraints: Evaluate returns 0; solve mode returns at least one update even if all surfaces are joint vacuum.

outputs.name: converged
outputs.description: Whether the solve stopping test passed, or whether evaluate mode completed without solving.
outputs.constraints: Always True in a returned mapping. In evaluate mode this does not assert ambipolar balance; solve failures raise.

preconditions: Positive magnetic magnitudes, mass, charge and thermal energies, finite compatible reference profiles and their declared SI units.
For solve mode, both reference densities are positive together or zero together at each surface, and the modeled flux ratio has a bracketable root within the bounded expansion.
supported: Independent scalar or vectorized flux-surface evaluation with prescribed potential and caller-defined density/temperature profiles.
Bounded solve of single-ion/electron charge-weighted end-loss balance, including mixed active and joint-vacuum surfaces.
excluded: A multispecies charge sum, collisional end-loss transport, self-consistent reference profiles or equilibrium reconstruction.
Interpreting evaluate-mode converged as a current-balance result, or claiming that a numerical root certifies the source model's physical validity.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for unsupported mode, nonfinite/nonpositive required scalar controls, refill values outside their mode-specific bounds, nonfinite or nonpositive fields/temperatures, negative densities, absent evaluate-mode phi_plug_v, or one-sided-vacuum solve surfaces. Noninteger max_iterations raises ValueError; incompatible broadcasts, numeric conversion and caller profile failures may raise ValueError or TypeError.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises RuntimeError when any active surface cannot be bracketed after eight bounded expansion rounds. Extreme finite inputs may overflow intermediate flux or bracket calculations; derived values have no general finiteness guard.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Raises RuntimeError when max_iterations expires without both midpoint-change and absolute log-current-ratio tests passing for all active surfaces; no best-effort result is returned.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No result mapping is returned after any validation, callback, bracketing or solve failure. Evaluate mode returns a complete diagnostic mapping even when the prescribed potential leaves a large current residual.

provenance.lineage_summary: SciRel-maintained relation corresponding to a saved Pleiades L1 mirror ambipolar end-loss operator, direct parity/analytic-limit regressions and maintained failure-semantic tests. Historical source/admission labels are development provenance, not current SciRel expert recognition.

python.signature: solve_mirror_ambipolar_potential(b_reference_t, b_plug_t, psi, ion_mass_kg, ion_charge_c, ion_density_ref_m3, ion_temperature_parallel_j, ion_temperature_perpendicular_j, electron_temperature_j, phi_reference_v=0.0, electron_density_ref_m3=None, ion_loss_refill=1.0, electron_loss_refill=1.0, potential_tolerance_v=1e-06, current_tolerance=1e-10, max_iterations=100, initial_bracket_thermal=8.0, mode='solve', phi_plug_v=None)

example.description: Check the zero-slope half-space barrier integral at a prescribed plug potential.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.closures import solve_mirror_ambipolar_potential
e = 1.602176634e-19
m_i = 1.67262192595e-27
m_e = 9.1093837139e-31
r = solve_mirror_ambipolar_potential(1.0, 1.0, 0.0, m_i, e, 2.0e18, 2.0*e, 3.0*e, e, electron_density_ref_m3=3.0e18, ion_loss_refill=0.25, electron_loss_refill=0.5, mode='evaluate', phi_plug_v=1.0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(r['ion_particle_flux_m2_s'], 2.0e18*np.sqrt(2.0*e/(2.0*np.pi*m_i))*np.exp(-0.5)*0.25)
np.testing.assert_allclose(r['electron_particle_flux_m2_s'], 3.0e18*np.sqrt(e/(2.0*np.pi*m_e))*0.5)
assert r['iterations'] == 0 and r['converged']
example.expected: The zero-mirror-slope ion barrier gives an exp(-1/2) factor, while the electron one-way flux has no barrier at +1 V; evaluate mode reports zero iterations without asserting current balance.

scope: An analytic zero-mirror-slope flux limit and selected vectorized, profile-callable and current-balance cases.
Joint-vacuum behavior, one-sided-vacuum rejection, invalid controls, bracket failure and iteration-budget nonconvergence.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct SciRel tests establish selected flux values from an independent half-space limit, reference-potential retention on joint vacuum, a convergent current-balance example, callable density profile equivalence, and selected failure paths. They do not prove the physical end-loss model, all pitch-integral branches, arbitrary parameter regimes, uniqueness of roots, final residual bounds at every extreme or current expert recognition.
known_limitations: Refill fractions and the prescribed reference profiles are external model inputs, not derived transport physics.
A successful evaluate call is not a current-balance solve; an extreme finite input may yield a nonfinite derived flux because no output finiteness check is applied.
The stop test uses the previous midpoint residual and the next midpoint change before final fluxes are recomputed.
Public distribution licensing and expert recognition remain pending.
